To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the addition of the highest fidelity system features, including a large field of regard, head-tracked rendering, and stereoscopic viewing, significantly improved the performance of participants in a spatial judgment task; 2) participants made significantly fewer spatial judgment errors when the system provided an increased field of view or when it included head-tracked rendering; and 3) participants were significantly faster in making spatial judgments when the system included stereoscopic viewing and head-tracked rendered images.
the use of stereo, head-tracked rendering, and a larger field of regard significantly improved participants' performance when making small-scale spatial judgements.
